title: Primary evidence audit of NylC critical and functionally tested residues
source_scope: Primary NylC mutagenesis, structure, substrate hydrolysis, maturation, assembly, and stability studies

alignment.method: Count nongap residues independently in the NylC 3AXG reference and the 328-residue Nyl12 alpha-plus-beta query; map via aligned columns, without a fixed offset.
alignment.reference: NylC_A/3AXG 355-aa reference, homolog mapping rather than a construct-specific structure alignment
alignment.limitations: For NylCp2 mutant literature, source construct numbering is assumed to match the 355-residue NylC reference numbering; NylC_A alleles differ at some sites. Homology assignment does not establish identical structure or mechanism.

sources.title: X-ray crystallographic and mutational analysis of the NylC precursor: catalytic mechanism of autocleavage and substrate hydrolysis of nylon hydrolase
sources.references: Table 1: local PDF p. 3/journal p. 3402; K189A discussion and Fig. 8: PDF pp. 11-12/journal pp. 3410-3411; Fig. 10: PDF p. 17/journal p. 3416; other figures/tables as cited per residue

sources.title: Three-dimensional structure of nylon hydrolase and mechanism of nylon-6 hydrolysis
Structural basis of the correct subunit assembly, aggregation, and intracellular degradation of nylon hydrolase

residues.evidence: N266A cleavage 42-57%; N266G 40-57%; variants remain partially processed. N266A/T267A double mutant <1% cleavage, but this does not isolate the N266 contribution.
residues.confidence: high for maturation sensitivity; none for independent substrate chemistry

residues.class: maturation nucleophile and proposed substrate nucleophile
residues.evidence: T267C in G122Y130 background <1% cleavage; N266A/T267A plus H130Y triple variant <1% (does not isolate T267A). T267S initially 9.7%, eventually >99% after 48 h (k=2.8e-5 s-1); cleavage-corrected activity 0.72 U/mg in G122Y130 background, with kcat/Km about 4% of its parental enzyme.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Mature substrate role is structurally and by analogy proposed; T267C/A low-activity results are confounded by failure to mature, and the A result is a triple mutant.
residues.confidence: high for maturation role; moderate for substrate nucleophile
residues.source: S1 Table 1, Figs. 3-4, Table 2; S2 Fig. 2

residues.evidence: D306A in NylCp2 and H-GYAQ and L137A/D306A in NylCA: <1% cleavage and <0.1 U/mg raw activity.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Asp306 is proposed in the substrate Asp308-Asp306-Thr267 triad; mutational loss of activity cannot isolate mature hydrolysis because cleavage fails. Proposed acid/base assignments are not directly observed.
residues.confidence: high for maturation requirement; low-to-moderate for mature substrate chemistry

residues.evidence: D308A in H-GYAQ: <1% cleavage and <0.1 U/mg raw activity.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Part of the proposed Asp308-Asp306-Thr267 mature-substrate triad; no mature D308A assay because precursor fails processing.
residues.confidence: high for H-GYAQ maturation requirement; low-to-moderate for mature substrate chemistry

residues.evidence: No G307 substitution tested in the audited NylC papers.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Backbone NH is proposed to stabilize the tetrahedral intermediate; this is model/structural inference.

residues.evidence: H-GYAQ K189A cleavage 6.0-33% (67-94% remains uncleaved); cleavage-normalized activity 0.032 U/mg (~0.6% parental). TLC: trace Ahx dimer after 24 h vs parental dimer and monomer by 1 h.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Severe effect persists after specific-activity/cleavage correction, supporting a role beyond maturation; exact chemistry (including proposed general-base or substrate-binding role) is not isolated from structural effects.
residues.confidence: high for important enzyme function and hydrolysis-associated role; moderate for exact mechanism
residues.source: S1 Table 1 footnote d (PDF p.3/journal p.3402), K189A discussion and Fig. 8 (PDF pp.11-12/journal pp.3410-3411), Fig. 10 (PDF p.17/journal p.3416), Fig. S12

residues.class: proposed oxyanion donor and side-chain hydrolysis contributor
residues.evidence: H-GYAQ Y146A cleavage 47-92%; cleavage-normalized activity 0.18 U/mg (~3.6% parental). NylCA Y146A kcat/Km reported ~3% parental; NylCA background carries L137A.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Alanine removes both aromatic ring and OH; no Y146F test. Backbone NH donor remains in Nyl12 F113, but its Tyr OH is absent.
residues.confidence: moderate-high for Tyr146 contribution; low for specific proton donation or F113 equivalence
residues.source: S1 Table 1 footnote d, Table 2, Figs. 8, 10, S13

residues.class: maturation water network; proposed oxyanion donor
residues.evidence: N219A precursor cleavage 31-33%; paper reports no cleavage-corrected mature N219A hydrolysis value.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Water-network participation in maturation supported; mature substrate oxyanion stabilization is proposed from structure, not isolated by mutant assay.
residues.confidence: high for maturation network involvement; low-to-moderate for mature substrate role

residues.evidence: F134A cleavage 44-59%; substrate activity not tested.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: No direct evidence of a mature-substrate chemical role.
residues.confidence: moderate for context-dependent maturation effect; low for catalysis

residues.class: assembly and maturation modifier, not catalytic-essential evidence
residues.evidence: NylCp2 L137A: <1% cleavage, <0.1 U/mg, Tm 41 vs 52 C; D122G partially rescues cleavage to 33-34%. NylCA naturally has A137 and is >99% cleaved.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Activity loss is confounded by altered oligomerization/maturation and is context-dependent; not evidence that Leu137 is an indispensable catalytic residue.
residues.confidence: high for context-dependent assembly/maturation effect; low for direct catalysis
residues.source: S1 Table 1; S2 Table 2; S3 Figs. 3-4, Table 1

residues.evidence: D122G raises Tm by ~22-24 C; D122G/H130Y double mutant remains active and improves apparent Ahx-oligomer affinity. D122 variants span active enzyme through failed expression/instability depending on substitution.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: No essential catalytic role; NylC-P2 D122G/H130Y effects are context-dependent interface and binding changes.
residues.confidence: high that it is not an established catalytic-essential site
residues.source: S2 Tables 1-2; S3 Tables 1-3; S1 Table 1

residues.evidence: H130Y raises Tm (~11 C); H130Y single mutant has lower measured Ahx activity than WT in reported assays, while combined G122Y130 restores/improves activity and substrate affinity.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Context-dependent effect; not established as catalytic-essential.
residues.confidence: high that thermostability is demonstrated; low for direct catalytic role

residues.evidence: D36A contributes only in combined thermostability constructs; no independent catalytic-essential test identified.
residues.confidence: low for direct function; high that it is not established essential

residues.evidence: E263Q appears in combined constructs that raise Tm; no evidence it is an essential catalytic residue.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Combination variants remain active; no isolated requirement shown.
residues.confidence: high that it is not established catalytic-essential

residues.evidence: G111S lowers Tm in NylCp2; NylCA carries the alternative Ser in an active enzyme.
residues.confidence: high that it is not established catalytic-essential

residues.evidence: V225M not expressed in one NylCp2 background; combined variants show context-dependent stability effects; natural NylCA carries Met.
residues.substrate_hydrolysis: Expression/stability effect, not a demonstrated catalytic role.
residues.confidence: high that it is not established catalytic-essential
